# Results {#sec-results}

Results are given at three levels: the country (national forest, all forest types together), each forest type, and each forest type within each administrative region. Forest types are those observed in the field, and plots that cover several forest types are split between them (@sec-methods). The country and forest type levels are presented in this section, and the forest type and region level in Annex 2.

- **ME** is the margin of error at the 90% confidence level, as a percentage of the estimate. It is not given for domains with a single plot.
- **Plots (n)** is the number of phase 2 clusters with at least one plot section in the domain. In the non-forest domain, it includes the phase 1 points of the non-forest stratum.
- Plot counts (threatened species, wildlife, disturbance, regeneration species frequency, NTFP availability and products) use the accessible field plots, assigned to the forest type of their main LULC section.
- At forest type and region level (Annex 2), many domains have few plots and the estimates are indicative only.
- The non-forest domain is only reported for areas. For the other results, the country level is the national forest: per hectare values are per hectare of forest, totals are totals of the forest area, and plot counts use the forest plots.

## Biological Diversity

### Tree Species Composition and Diversity

<!-- IVI, Shannon index keep the top 10 or 20. We can do it by species and genus and family -->

The Importance Value Index (IVI) is the sum of the relative density, relative frequency and relative dominance (basal area) of each taxon, from 0 to 300. Density and basal area are two-phase estimates. Frequency is the number of plot sections where the taxon is recorded. Unidentified trees are not included.

The tables give the top 10 taxa by IVI, with the relative density, frequency and dominance that make up the index. The top 20 species, genera and families are in Annex 3.

The most important species at country level are shown in @fig-ivi-species and @tbl-ivi-species-country, and in each forest type in @fig-ivi-species-ftype and `r ftype_ref(tab$b_ivi_species, "ivi-species")`. Genera are in @tbl-ivi-genus-country and `r ftype_ref(tab$b_ivi_genus, "ivi-genus")`, families in @tbl-ivi-family-country and `r ftype_ref(tab$b_ivi_family, "ivi-family")`, and the Shannon index in @tbl-shannon-country, @tbl-shannon-ftype and @fig-shannon. The same tables by forest type and region are in Annex 2.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ivi-species
#| fig-cap: "Top 20 species by Importance Value Index, country level."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 5.8
fig$b_ivi_species
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ivi-species-ftype
#| fig-cap: "Top 10 species by Importance Value Index in each forest type."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 8.5
fig$b_ivi_species_ftype
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-shannon
#| fig-cap: "Shannon index of tree species by forest type and region. Error bars: 90% confidence interval."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
fig$b_shannon
```

```{r}

#| include: false
## IVI tables: IVI and its relative components only
ivi_drop <- c("n_pp", "density", "density_mep", "basal_area", "n_sections")
```

```{r}

#| results: asis
print_levels(top_n_levels(tab$b_ivi_species, 10), "ivi-species", "Top 10 species by Importance Value Index", .heading = "#####", .drop = ivi_drop, .split_ftype = TRUE)
```


```{r}

```

#### Shannon diversity index

The Shannon index $H'$ is computed from the estimated density of each taxon in the domain, at species, genus and family level. Richness is the number of taxa recorded, and evenness is $H' / \ln(\text{richness})$.

```{r}
#| label: 03-shannon-table
#| results: asis
print_levels(tab$b_shannon, "shannon", "Shannon diversity index", .heading = "#####")
```

### Rare, Threatened and Endangered Tree Species

<!-- Check the whole species list against the IUCN checklist. -->

Tree species are matched with the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species (version published on GBIF, `r format(info$iucn_date, "%B %Y")`). Threatened species are in the categories Critically Endangered (CR), Endangered (EN) and Vulnerable (VU). Occurrence is the number of accessible field plots with at least one live tree of the species (@fig-iucn, @tbl-iucn-country and @tbl-iucn-ftype, and by region `r annex_ref(tab$c_iucn, "iucn")` in Annex 2). The full list of recorded tree species, with their IUCN category, is in Annex 4 (@tbl-species-list).

```{r}
#| label: fig-iucn
#| fig-cap: "Number of plots with threatened tree species, by forest type."

fig$c_iucn
```

```{r}

#| results: asis
print_levels(tab$c_iucn, "iucn", "Tree species in the IUCN Red List threatened categories", .drop = "tree_iucn_category")
```

#### Frequency of occurrence of wildlife species

```{r}
#| label: 03-wildlife-values
#| include: false
wl_list   <- tab$d_wildlife_list
wl_n_sp   <- sum(!is.na(wl_list$wildlife_sci_name))
wl_pct_id <- round(sum(wl_list$n_records[!is.na(wl_list$wildlife_sci_name)]) / sum(wl_list$n_records) * 100)
wl_top    <- tab$d_wildlife_freq$country |> slice_max(n_plots, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE)
wl_iucn   <- tab$d_wildlife_iucn$country
```

The wildlife records are presence-only, so the species are compared by their frequency of occurrence instead of an IVI or Shannon index (@sec-wildlife-analysis). `r wl_n_sp` species are identified, accounting for `r wl_pct_id`% of the records; the other records are not identified to species. The most frequent species are *`r wl_top$wildlife_sci_name[1]`*, *`r wl_top$wildlife_sci_name[2]`* and *`r wl_top$wildlife_sci_name[3]`*, recorded in `r wl_top$pct_plots[1]`%, `r wl_top$pct_plots[2]`% and `r wl_top$pct_plots[3]`% of the plots (@tbl-wildlife-freq-country and @tbl-wildlife-freq-ftype, top 10 species). The full list of species is in Annex 4 (@tbl-wildlife-list).

```{r}

#| results: asis
```


## Forest Health and Vitality

### Tree Health and Condition

<!-- percentage of healthy / damage trees. -->

At country level, `r tab$e_health$country$pct_healthy`% of the trees are healthy (@tbl-health-country). The condition classes are in @fig-condition, @tbl-condition-country and @tbl-condition-ftype, and by region in `r annex_ref(tab$e_health, "health")` and `r annex_ref(tab$e_condition, "condition")` (Annex 2).

#### Crown condition

```{r}
#| label: 03-crown-values
#| include: false
crown_ctry <- tab$e_crown$country |> mutate(tree_condition_crown_label = as.character(tree_condition_crown_label)) |> split(~tree_condition_crown_label)
cause_ctry <- tab$e_cause$country |> filter(tree_cause != "Not recorded") |> arrange(desc(pct_damaged))
sev_ctry   <- tab$e_cause_severity$country |>
  filter(tree_condition_overall_label != "Slightly affected", tree_cause != "Not recorded", tree_cause != "Animals", tree_cause != "Other") |>
  summarise(pct = sum(pct), .by = tree_cause) |>
  arrange(desc(pct))
```

The crown condition of the live trees is assessed separately from their overall condition, from the foliage, dieback and structural damage of the crown. At country level, `r crown_ctry$Healthy$pct`% of the live trees have a healthy crown and `r crown_ctry[["Declining health"]]$pct`% a crown in declining health (@fig-crown, @tbl-crown-country and @tbl-crown-ftype). Results by region are in `r annex_ref(tab$e_crown, "crown")` (Annex 2).

```{r}

#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4

```

```{r}

#| results: asis
print_levels(tab$e_crown, "crown", "Tree density by crown condition class", .heading = "#####")
```

#### Causes of damage

The causes of damage are recorded for the damaged trees, and a tree can have several causes. Each cause is estimated separately, as the density of the damaged trees with this cause, and its shares of the live trees and of the damaged trees do not add up to 100%. Damaged trees without a recorded cause are reported as "Not recorded". At country level, the most frequent causes are `r str_to_lower(cause_ctry$tree_cause[1])`, `r str_to_lower(cause_ctry$tree_cause[2])` and `r str_to_lower(cause_ctry$tree_cause[3])`, recorded on `r cause_ctry$pct_damaged[1]`%, `r cause_ctry$pct_damaged[2]`% and `r cause_ctry$pct_damaged[3]`% of the damaged trees (@tbl-cause-country and @tbl-cause-ftype). Results by region are in `r annex_ref(tab$e_cause, "cause")` (Annex 2). The causes are attributed from visible symptoms in the field, and decline without an obvious agent may be recorded as disease.

```{r}
#| label: 03-cause-table
#| results: asis
print_levels(tab$e_cause, "cause", "Density of damaged trees by recorded cause of damage", .heading = "#####")
```

#### Causes and severity of damage

The severity of the damage is the overall condition of the damaged trees. Most damaged trees are slightly affected, whatever the cause. The share of severely affected or dying trees is highest for `r str_to_lower(sev_ctry$tree_cause[1])` (`r sev_ctry$pct[1]`%) and lowest for `r str_to_lower(last(sev_ctry$tree_cause))` (`r last(sev_ctry$pct)`%) at country level (@fig-cause-severity, @tbl-cause-severity-country and @tbl-cause-severity-ftype).

```{r}
#| label: fig-cause-severity
#| fig-cap: "Density of damaged trees by recorded cause and severity of the damage, country level. A tree with several causes is counted for each cause."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
fig$e_cause_severity
```

```{r}
#| label: 03-cause-severity
#| results: asis
print_levels(tab$e_cause_severity, "cause-severity", "Damaged trees by recorded cause and severity of the damage", .heading = "#####")
```

### Deadwood and Litter

```{r}
#| label: 03-deadwood-values
#| include: false
dw_ctry <- tab$m_dw_standing$country |> mutate(dw_decomposition = as.character(dw_decomposition)) |> split(~dw_decomposition)
stump_ctry <- tab$m_stump$country |> mutate(dw_decomposition = as.character(dw_decomposition)) |> split(~dw_decomposition)
```

Standing deadwood (dead standing trees with DBH of at least 10 cm) is measured with the live trees, and its stem volume is calculated as for the live trees. At country level, there are `r dw_ctry$Total$stems_ha` dead standing stems/ha, for `r dw_ctry$Total$dw_volume_ha` m³/ha (@tbl-dw-standing-country and @tbl-dw-standing-ftype). The decomposition status is not recorded for most dead standing trees. Stumps (diameter of at least 10 cm) are also measured with the live trees, and their volume is calculated as a cylinder from their diameter and height: there are `r stump_ctry$Total$stems_ha` stumps/ha, for `r stump_ctry$Total$dw_volume_ha` m³/ha (@tbl-stump-country and @tbl-stump-ftype). Lying deadwood is measured along the 20 m transect of each plot, and its volume estimated with the line-intersect method (@tbl-dw-lying-country and @tbl-dw-lying-ftype). Results by forest type and region are in `r annex_ref(tab$m_dw_standing, "dw-standing")`, `r annex_ref(tab$m_stump, "stump")` and `r annex_ref(tab$m_dw_lying, "dw-lying")` (Annex 2).

Litter depth is observed in the litter subplot, in classes. The shares of area by depth class are two-phase estimates, using the plots with a litter observation (@fig-litter, @tbl-litter-country and @tbl-litter-ftype).

### Forest Regeneration

```{r}
#| label: 03-regen-values
#| include: false
regen_ctry <- tab$j_regen$country |> mutate(regen_class = as.character(regen_class)) |> split(~regen_class)
```

Seedlings (height below 1.3 m) and saplings (height of at least 1.3 m and DBH below 10 cm) of tree species are counted in the regeneration subplot of each plot, two-phase estimates (@sec-est-plot-records). At country level, the regeneration density is `r format(regen_ctry$Total$regen_ha, big.mark = ",")` individuals/ha (ME `r regen_ctry$Total$regen_mep`%), with `r format(regen_ctry$Seedlings$regen_ha, big.mark = ",")` seedlings/ha and `r format(regen_ctry$Saplings$regen_ha, big.mark = ",")` saplings/ha (@tbl-regen-country). Densities by forest type are in @fig-regen and @tbl-regen-ftype, and by forest type and region in `r annex_ref(tab$j_regen, "regen")` (Annex 2). Richness is the number of identified species recorded in the accessible field plots of the domain.

The main species of the regeneration are in @tbl-regen-species-country and @tbl-regen-species-ftype. Relative density is the share of the species in the total regeneration density of the domain, and plots with record the share of accessible field plots with at least one seedling or sapling of the species.

```{r}

#| fig-cap: "Density of seedlings and saplings by forest type and region. Error bars: 90% confidence interval."
```


## Productive Functions of Forests

### Non-Timber Forest Products

```{r}
#| label: 03-ntfp-values
#| include: false
ntfp_ftype <- tab$k_ntfp$forest_type |> filter(ntfp_use == "Any NTFP") |> split(~forest_type)
```

NTFPs are recorded in the main plot with their use categories and their availability (few, moderate, abundant), without quantities. The share of the area with at least one NTFP is the indicator of the productive function of forests for NTFPs, two-phase estimates (@sec-est-plot-records). NTFPs are found on `r ntfp_ftype[["Closed Forest"]]$area_ntfp_pct`% of the closed forest area and `r ntfp_ftype[["Open Forest"]]$area_ntfp_pct`% of the open forest area, and were not recorded in mangrove forest (@fig-ntfp, @tbl-ntfp-country and @tbl-ntfp-ftype). Results by forest type and region are in `r annex_ref(tab$k_ntfp, "ntfp")` (Annex 2).

The accessible field plots with NTFP are counted by the highest availability recorded for each use category in @tbl-ntfp-avail-country and @tbl-ntfp-avail-ftype, and by forest type and region in `r annex_ref(tab$k_ntfp_avail, "ntfp-avail")` (Annex 2). The most frequent products are in @tbl-ntfp-product-country and @tbl-ntfp-product-ftype.


### Forest Biomass and Carbon Stocks

#### Aboveground biomass

```{r}
#| label: 03-biomass-values
#| include: false
agb_ctry <- tab$i_biomass$country |> mutate(tree_group = as.character(tree_group)) |> split(~tree_group)
```

Aboveground biomass (AGB) of live trees is estimated with the allometric equation of @chave2014. AGB per hectare is the ratio estimate of the domain, and the total AGB is the AGB per hectare times the domain area. Baobabs (*Adansonia digitata*) are reported separately: their AGB is calculated with the same equation, from their measured height and wood density, but the equation is not calibrated for their water-storing stem and these values are indicative only. Each table gives the trees without baobab, the baobabs alone and all trees together.

At country level, AGB is `r format(agb_ctry[["All trees"]]$agb_ha, nsmall = 1)` t/ha for all trees (ME `r agb_ctry[["All trees"]]$agb_ha_mep`%), of which `r format(agb_ctry[["Trees without baobab"]]$agb_ha, nsmall = 1)` t/ha for trees without baobab and `r format(agb_ctry[["Baobab"]]$agb_ha, nsmall = 1)` t/ha for baobabs (@fig-biomass-ftype and @tbl-biomass-country). Results by forest type are in @fig-biomass-ftype and @tbl-biomass-ftype, and by forest type and region in @fig-biomass and `r annex_ref(tab$i_biomass, "biomass")` (Annex 2).

```{r}
#| label: fig-biomass-ftype
#| fig-cap: "Aboveground biomass of trees without baobab and of baobabs, country level and by forest type. Error bars: 90% confidence interval of all trees, n = number of plots."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
fig$i_biomass_ftype
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-biomass
#| fig-cap: "Aboveground biomass of trees without baobab and of baobabs, by forest type and region. Error bars: 90% confidence interval of all trees, n = number of plots."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
fig$i_biomass
```

The variability of AGB between field clusters is shown in @fig-biomass-cluster: each point is the AGB of all trees in the part of a cluster in the forest type.

```{r}
#| label: fig-biomass-cluster
#| fig-cap: "Aboveground biomass of all trees by field cluster and forest type. Points: clusters, n = number of clusters."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
fig$i_biomass_cluster
```

```{r}
#| label: 03-biomass-table
#| results: asis
print_levels(tab$i_biomass, "biomass", "Aboveground biomass", .heading = "#####")
```

#### Carbon stocks

```{r}
#| label: 03-carbon-values
#| include: false
c_ctry <- tab$n_carbon$country |> mutate(pool = as.character(pool)) |> split(~pool)
```

Carbon stocks are the biomass of each pool times the carbon fraction of 0.47 [@ipcc2006]. Belowground biomass is the AGB times the IPCC default root-to-shoot ratio of the forest type: 0.49 for mangrove forest [@ipcc2014] and 0.332 for the closed and open forests [tropical dry forest, @ipcc2019], applied to the whole country (@sec-biomass-analysis). Deadwood biomass is estimated from the volumes of standing deadwood, stumps and lying deadwood, with the wood density and the density reduction factor of the decomposition status (@sec-biomass-analysis). Litter mass is not measured, and litter carbon uses the IPCC Tier 1 defaults of mature forests: 2.4 t C/ha for the closed and open forests [tropical dry forest, @ipcc2019] and 0.7 t C/ha for mangrove forest [@ipcc2014]. The uncertainty of the total combines the uncertainties of the pools with IPCC approach 1 (@sec-biomass-analysis).

At country level, the total carbon stock is `r c_ctry$Total$carbon_ha` t C/ha (ME `r c_ctry$Total$carbon_ha_mep`%), or `r format(round(c_ctry$Total$carbon_tot / 1e6, 2), nsmall = 2)` million t C in the forest area (@fig-carbon, @tbl-carbon-country and @tbl-carbon-ftype). Results by forest type and region are in `r annex_ref(tab$n_carbon, "carbon")` (Annex 2).

```{r}
#| label: fig-carbon
#| fig-cap: "Carbon stocks by pool, country level and forest types. Error bars: 90% confidence interval of the total (IPCC approach 1)."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4.3
fig$n_carbon
```

```{r}
#| label: 03-carbon-table
#| results: asis
print_levels(tab$n_carbon, "carbon", "Carbon stocks by pool", .heading = "#####")
```

## Protective Functions of Forests

### Soil Condition and Characteristics

Soil surface condition, organic layer depth, topsoil and subsoil texture, and topsoil colour are observed at the measurement point of each plot (visual soil assessment). The shares of area in each class are two-phase estimates, using the plots with an observation of the attribute (@sec-est-plot-records). Results are given for the national forest (country level) and by forest type (@fig-soil, @tbl-soil-country and @tbl-soil-ftype). Soil results are not given by region. They describe site conditions and are not direct measures of soil fertility or degradation.

```{r}
#| label: fig-soil
#| fig-cap: "Share of area by soil class, all forest (country level) and forest types."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 5.5
fig$l_soil
```

```{r}
#| label: 03-soil-table
#| results: asis
print_levels(tab$l_soil, "soil", "Share of area by soil class")
```
